intent: The arrow at the top edge of a Select popup that scrolls the option list up while the pointer rests on it.
typical_uses: The top scroll affordance SelectContent renders before its list

dont_use_when.situation: A scrolling region of a page or a panel, outside any select

invariants.text: The arrow is in the DOM only while the list can scroll further up and the popup was not opened by touch, unless `keepMounted` is true.
Moving the pointer over the arrow scrolls the list up one option at a time until the pointer leaves or the list reaches its top edge; the arrow is `aria-hidden` and takes no focus.

anti_patterns.dont: Add a SelectScrollUpButton as a child of SelectContent
anti_patterns.do_instead: Leave it out; SelectContent already renders one, and a child lands inside the list as a second arrow over the first

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the arrow's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the arrow's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (typed as an empty object for an arrow). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through select.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A popup whose built-in arrows appear once the list overflows

bad.title: The arrow added again inside the popup
bad.why: SelectContent renders its own SelectScrollUpButton; this one is mounted inside the list, so two arrows compete for the same edge.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, SelectScrollUpArrowState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through select.module.css, not through this.
